questions.question: A campus network wires every building's LAN as a star but interconnects the three building switches in a ring. Which topology class does this design belong to?
questions.explanation: The design combines two distinct topologies - star inside each building and ring between them - which by definition makes the overall layout a hybrid topology rather than any single pure form.

questions.question: A link has 10 Mbps bandwidth and a 50 ms round-trip time. What is its bandwidth-delay product in bits?
questions.explanation: BDP = bandwidth x RTT = 10,000,000 x 0.05 = 500,000 bits, the maximum data in transit.

questions.question: A vendor's training material maps 'encryption and compression' to layer 6, 'routing' to layer 3, and 'bits on the wire' to layer 1 of a seven-layer reference model. Which model is it describing?
questions.explanation: Only the OSI reference model is a seven-layer stack in which layer 6 (Presentation) owns encryption/compression, layer 3 (Network) routes, and layer 1 (Physical) moves raw bits.

questions.question: Unlike the seven-layer reference model, the suite the Internet actually runs on collapses the top three layers into a single Application layer, leaving four layers total. Which protocol suite is this?
questions.explanation: The practical Internet stack is the four-layer TCP/IP suite (Link, Internet, Transport, Application); OSI's Session, Presentation, and Application functions are merged into its top layer.

questions.question: To shrink broadcast domains and apply different firewall policies per department, an administrator divides 10.0.0.0/16 into smaller prefix blocks. What is this practice called?
questions.explanation: Borrowing host bits to carve one large network into smaller segments - each with its own broadcast domain and policy boundary - is subnetting.

questions.question: An ISP advertises a link by how many bits it can transmit each second - one hundred million on this service. Which metric describes that quantity?
questions.explanation: Bits transmitted per unit of time is the definition of bit rate (data rate); bandwidth, baud, and throughput are related but distinct terms.

questions.question: A UDP application sends each packet independently - no connection state, no ordering guarantee, no retransmission. What is this self-contained, independently routed delivery unit called?
questions.explanation: Connectionless protocols treat every unit as self-contained with its own addressing and no relationship to previous units - the definition of a datagram.

questions.question: On a legacy LAN, a station may transmit only while it holds a special permission frame that circulates from station to station around the loop. Which network architecture is this?
questions.explanation: Passing a circulating 'token' frame that grants the right to transmit is the media-access method of Token Ring (IEEE 802.5), the classic deterministic alternative to Ethernet.

questions.question: Hosts addressed 192.168.0.0/16 reach the Internet after the gateway rewrites each outbound packet's source address to its own public IP. Which technique is performing this rewrite?
questions.explanation: Translating private RFC 1918 source addresses into a public routable address (and back on the return path) at the gateway is NAT.

questions.question: A laptop joins an unfamiliar network and, after a four-packet exchange, automatically receives its IP address, mask, default gateway, and DNS servers. Which protocol supplied them?
questions.explanation: Automatic delivery of IP, mask, gateway, and DNS via the Discover-Offer-Request-Acknowledge sequence is DHCP's job; manual assignment or APIPA would not consult a server.

questions.question: A lab wants every router cabled directly to every other router. For n routers, each connects to n-1 peers and every link gets counted twice. Which expression gives the true number of links?
questions.explanation: Each of n nodes needs n-1 links, giving n(n-1) endpoints, but every link is shared by two nodes, so divide by 2: n(n-1)/2, the same as the combination C(n,2).

questions.question: How many links are required for a full mesh of 10 devices?
questions.explanation: 10(10-1)/2 = 45 links in a full mesh.

questions.question: A ping across a satellite hop shows a high RTT dominated by the time the signal physically takes to cross 72,000 km - not by serialization or queueing. Which delay component dominates this RTT?
questions.explanation: Propagation delay = distance / signal speed and is unavoidable on long links; serialization (transmission), processing, and queueing delays are unrelated to physical distance.

questions.question: To size a TCP window so a 1 Gbps link with a 50 ms RTT never goes idle, engineers multiply the bandwidth by the delay. What is this product called?
questions.explanation: The bandwidth-delay product tells how many bits can be 'in flight' before the first ACK returns; the send window must reach the BDP to keep a fat, long link saturated.

questions.question: A museum's half-duplex 10BASE2 segment still forces stations to listen before transmitting and to abort when two stations transmit at once. Which media-access method is this?
alternatives: Carrier Sense Multiple Access with Collision Detection
questions.explanation: Listen-first (carrier sense), shared medium (multiple access), and abort-on-simultaneous-transmit (collision detection) is CSMA/CD - classic Ethernet's half-duplex access method.

questions.question: A 10 Mbit file is transmitted over a 2 Mbps link, ignoring all overhead. How many seconds does the transmission take?
questions.explanation: Transmission delay = file size / bandwidth = 10 Mbit / 2 Mbps = 5 s.

questions.question: A signal travels 3,000 km through optical fiber at a propagation speed of 2 x 10^8 m/s. What is the propagation delay in milliseconds?
questions.explanation: Propagation delay = distance / speed = 3,000,000 m / 200,000,000 m/s = 0.015 s = 15 ms.

questions.question: According to the Nyquist theorem, what is the maximum symbol rate (in baud) of a noiseless channel with a 4 kHz bandwidth?
questions.explanation: Nyquist sets the maximum symbol rate at twice the bandwidth: 2 x 4 kHz = 8000 baud.

questions.question: What is the bandwidth-delay product of a 20 Mbps link with a round-trip time of 100 ms?
questions.explanation: BDP = bandwidth x delay = 20 x 10^6 bit/s x 0.1 s = 2 x 10^6 bits, the maximum data in flight.

questions.question: A full-mesh network has exactly 15 links. How many devices does it contain?
questions.explanation: Solving n(n-1)/2 = 15 gives n(n-1) = 30, so n = 6 devices.
